question: m01
q: Are real wages going up? Compare wage growth from the ABS Wage Price Index with inflation.

transcript.answer:
**Real wages are falling again. Wage growth has slipped below inflation since late 2025, and the gap has widened over 2026.**

**Latest figures**
- **Wages:** The Wage Price Index (total hourly pay excluding bonuses, seasonally adjusted) rose 3.2% in the year to June quarter 2026. That matches March quarter 2026, and it is down from 4.1% in June quarter 2024.
- **Inflation:** Headline CPI was 3.8% in the year to June 2026 and 4.0% in the year to August 2026. Trimmed mean, the RBA's preferred underlying measure, was 3.6% in both June and August 2026.
- **Real wage growth:** In June 2026 it was about **-0.6 percentage points** (3.2% wages minus 3.8% CPI). Against underlying inflation it was about -0.4 points (3.2% minus 3.6%).

**Wage growth against inflation, year-on-year**

| Quarter | WPI | CPI (headline) | Approx. real wage growth |
|---|---|---|---|
| Jun 2025 | 3.4% | 1.9% (monthly CPI), 2.1% (quarterly CPI) | about +1.3 to +1.5 |
| Sep 2025 | 3.3% | 3.6% (monthly CPI), 3.2% (quarterly CPI) | about -0.3 to +0.1 |
| Dec 2025 | 3.4% | 3.8% | about -0.4 |
| Mar 2026 | 3.2% | 4.6% | about -1.4 |
| Jun 2026 | 3.2% | 3.8% | about -0.6 |

CPI figures are for the last month of each quarter. For Jun and Sep 2025 I show both the monthly and quarterly CPI series, since they differ.

**What this shows**
- Real wages grew during the first half of 2025, when inflation fell to about 2% and wages were still rising at about 3.4%.
- Inflation then rebounded to 3.5–4.6% from the second half of 2025, while wage growth stayed at about 3.2–3.4%. That put real wages in negative territory from late 2025.
- The gap was widest in March 2026, when CPI hit 4.6%.
- The August 2026 CPI of 4.0% is higher than the June wage growth of 3.2%. Unless wage growth picks up, the September quarter WPI, due in November, is likely to show real wages still falling.

**Caveat:** The WPI measures pay for the same jobs, so it excludes promotions and job changes. Real average earnings and household incomes can differ, and so can the effect on any one household, because CPI is an average basket.
